raw_response:
I am 60 years old and I have farmed these 2 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. My wife and son help me when they are free from other work. It is not much land, but it is what we have, so I watch every yuan I spend.

For wheat, I sowed last October after running the rotary tiller. I plant Luyuan 502 — that is what Old Wang down the road plants, and his wheat always looks full and does not fall over. For my 2 mu, I put down two 50-kilogram bags of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as base fertilizer before sowing, that is 50 kg per mu. At green-up in spring and again at jointing, I top-dress with urea: 10 kg per mu each time, so 20 kg per mu total. That works out to about 17 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus per mu, and 6 kg of potassium per mu from the compound bag. I irrigate four times: the overwinter water I already did before freeze-up, once at jointing when the ears are forming, once at heading, and once at grain filling. I spray three times — herbicide once when the wheat was at the three-leaf stage last autumn, and insecticide twice this spring and early summer, once when the red spiders show up and once at heading if I see aphids. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu. This year I expect 500 kg per mu if the spring wind does not dry out the heads.

For summer maize, I will plant Denghai 605 right after the wheat combine leaves the field in mid-June. I do not till for maize — I use the no-till planter to save diesel and time, because the wheat stubble is still in the field and the soil is hard enough. For base fertilizer I will put down 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, that is 80 kg for my 2 mu. When the plants reach the big trumpet stage, I will top-dress with 25 kg per mu of urea. That comes to about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus per mu, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. Maize only needs two irrigations here: one when it is knee-high, and one at grain filling. I will spray twice — herbicide after emergence, and once for corn borer when I see the moths flying in July. I expect 550 kg per mu; last year I got about 530 kg.

With only 2 mu, I cannot afford to gamble. If I am unsure whether to add more fertilizer, I add it. Losing 50 kg of grain costs me more than an extra 40-kilogram bag of urea. I do what my neighbors do, and I do what I did last year. Change is risk.
